paragraphs.source_en: This time the shell fired by the enemy was aimed with precision; it flew over the lattice fence, shook down the paulownia leaves with a rustle, and struck the bamboo fence of the second rampart. What a tremendous sound it made! Newton's first law of motion says: "Unless acted upon by an external force, a body once set in motion proceeds in a straight line at a uniform velocity." If bodies moved only according to that formula of motion, the master's head would probably by now have shared the fate of Aeschylus's head. Fortunately, after inventing the first formula Newton also devised the second, and so the master's head escaped with its life at the critical instant. Newton's second law of motion says: "The change of motion is proportional to the force applied, and occurs along the straight line in which that force acts." What exactly this means is somewhat hard to understand. But judging from the fact that the dum-dum bullet pierced the bamboo fence, tore through the paper sliding door, and still failed to smash the master's head, he must certainly have Newton to thank. After a while, just as expected, someone seemed to have burst into the garden, saying, "Is it here?" "Probably farther to the left!" At the same time there came the sound of someone beating about the dwarf bamboo with a stick. Whenever the enemy bursts into the master's garden to retrieve a dum-dum bullet, they always make an especially loud racket. If they slipped in quietly and picked it up quietly, they would fail to achieve their chief objective. The dum-dum bullet may be precious, but teasing the master is more important than the dum-dum bullet. In fact, they can make out from a distance where the shell has landed; they can tell from the sound that it hit the bamboo wall, and they know perfectly well where it struck, so if they went about it properly they could retrieve it without any difficulty. According to Leibniz's definition, space is an order capable of completing phenomena of coexistence. A, B, C, and D appear at all times in the same sequence. There are bound to be loaches under the willow shade; bats are inseparable from the moon; a ball against the foot of a wall may be an awkward pairing, but those who throw a ball into someone else's garden every day have grown used to this spatial arrangement, and can tell at a glance where the ball is. Their making such an uproar is nothing more than a strategy for matching themselves against the master, who can only suffer the attack passively.

paragraphs.source_zh: 这一次敌军打来的炮弹瞄得很准，它从方格篱笆上飞过来打得桐树叶子簌簌散落，命中了第二道城墙的竹编篱笆上。好大的一个声响！牛顿的第一运动律曰：“如不加以外力，一旦开始运动的物体则以同等速度直线向前运动。”如果物体只按这个运动公式来运行的话，那么主人的头恐怕这时会和伊斯基拉斯的头落入同一命运。所幸牛顿在发明第一公式之后还造出了第二公式，所以主人的头在千钧一发之际总算保住了。牛顿的运动第二公式曰：“运动的变化与所加的外力成正比，而且产生于其力所作用的直线上。”这到底是说什么，有点不容易弄懂。不过从达姆达姆弹穿透竹篱笆、撞破纸拉门而未能敲碎主人的头来看，他肯定是托了牛顿的福。又过了一会儿，果然不出所料，有人闯进院子里来，一边说着：“是这儿吗？”“恐怕还要靠左！”一边发出用棍子敲打矮竹丛的声音。每次敌人闯进主人的院子里来拣达姆达姆弹的时候，总是要发出特别大的声音。如果悄悄进来、悄悄拣走，那就达不到最主要的目的了。达姆达姆弹可能是贵重的，不过捉弄主人则要比达姆达姆弹更为重要。其实，他们从远处就能弄清炮弹的着弹地，打中竹墙的声音也听得出，打中哪里也清楚得很，所以只要规规矩矩去拣，完全可以拣回来的。根据莱布尼兹的定义，空间是能完成同在现象的一种秩序。甲乙丙丁在任何时候都是按同一顺序出现的。柳荫下一定会有泥鳅，蝙蝠离不开月亮，墙根上配一个球也许不协调，但是在每天都把球扔进别人家院子里来的人，他们已经习惯于这种空间排列，只要一看就会发现球在哪里。他们如此折腾，无非是出于要和被动挨打的主人一决雌雄的策略罢了。
